cards.explanation: The answer is Annas, friends. He's Caiaphas's father-in-law, so the family tree is doing some work in this story. The text says they bring Jesus to him first, before anyone else. Caiaphas is the high priest that year (John 18:13).

The answer is that it would be better if one man died for the people. That's the advice, word for word from the text. Caiaphas said it would be better if one man died for the people. Notice he said “died.” That one word makes this a heavy line, and I think it's worth slowing down for.

The answer is True, friends. The other disciple goes in with Jesus because the high priest knows him. Peter stays outside at the door. He's standing out there like someone who showed up to the party without the invite.

The answer is that he says he is not. Peter answers, “I am not…” That's a short answer to a short question, and it's a hard one to read. I think this is where the story gets heavy. Hold on to it, friends, because it comes back.

The answer is cold, friends. The text says that because it was cold, the servants and officers made a charcoal fire to keep warm. Peter's standing with them, warming himself. A fire on a cold night is the oldest idea there is.
The answer is teaching. The high priest asks Jesus about His disciples and His teaching. Two things are on the table. Jesus answers next, so listen to that.

The answer is those who heard His message, friends. Jesus says, “Ask those who heard My message. Surely they know what I said.” He taught openly, so there were plenty of people to ask. He doesn't point the high priest to anyone in secret.

The answer is that He asks why He was struck if He spoke correctly. Jesus replies, “If I said something wrong, testify as to what was wrong. But if I spoke correctly, why did you strike Me?” It's a plain question. This is a heavy moment, and Jesus answers it straight.
The answer is False, friends. By the fire they ask him, “Aren’t you also one of His disciples?” and he denies it. He says, “I am not…” It's a heavy moment, and the text doesn't hide it.

The answer is that a rooster crows, friends. The text says Peter denied it once more, and immediately a rooster crowed. Earlier Jesus told Peter that the rooster wouldn't crow before Peter denied Him three times (John 13:38). That's the sound that follows.
